tools.description:
Descriptions:
  Analyses all devices in a home and returns the device inventory (status, battery level, tamper state, categories, room and capabilities) so that actionable maintenance and optimisation recommendations can be generated from the real device state.

When to use:
  Used when the user asks for recommendations, tips, health checks or "what should I do" about their home devices.

Guidelines:
  When presenting this information to the user, it should be a concise and actionable set of device recommendations.
  Group recommendations into the following categories: URGENT, PREVENT, OPTIMIZATION, SECURITY.
  Omit any category that has no relevant recommendations.
  Use URGENT for critical issues needing immediate action, such as battery at or below 15%, devices offline, or active tamper alerts.
  Use PREVENT for preventive maintenance, such as batteries between 16% and 40%, devices that have not communicated recently, or checking controllers, hubs and signal quality.
  Use OPTIMIZATION for optimisation suggestions, such as camera recording or SD card configuration, motion sensitivity, schedules, timers, or energy savings for devices left on.
  Use SECURITY for security suggestions, such as arming the system when away, keeping tamper state verified, or reviewing security devices.
  Reference each device by its name and, when useful, include the battery percentage or status.
  Don't include unnecessary details.
  Don't list all devices available, instead return only insights and recommendations for the relevant devices.
tools.name: get_device_recommendations

outputSchema.description: Tool response. On failure the response contains a structured error.

tools.title: Devices Recommendations

Description:
  Retrieve home status brief

When to use:
  Use when the user wants to get a brief status of the home. Authentication is handled internally by the MCP server.

Guidelines:
  When presenting this information to the user, it should be a brief summary of the home's status, including whether the alarm is armed and its current status

  Try to keep the information concise and easy to understand.

  Update the alarm security state from the user home.

When to use:
  Use to change the security status from the user home. Authentication is handled internally by the MCP server.
  For a mode change, use status disarm, stay or away with armDelay: [] and alarmDelay: [].

tools.description:
Description:
  Find a device by natural language name or description and update one of its capabilities in a single operation.

When to use:
  Use when the user refers to a device by a descriptive or colloquial name (e.g. "living room light", "bedroom AC") and wants to change (e.g., power, brightness, temperature, color) a specific capability of a device.

How to use:
  On the body Capability update payload:
    -Use type='power' to turn on/off (value: 'on' or 'off').
    -Use type='brightness' to change light level (value: 0-100 number).
    -Use type='temperature' to set temperature (value: numeric degrees).
    -Use type='color_rgb' to change color (redValue, greenValue, blueValue: 0-255).
    -The 'type' field is the discriminator — pick it based on what the user asked to change.

body.description: Capability update payload. Use type='power' to turn on/off (value: 'on' or 'off'). Use type='brightness' to change light level (value: 0-100 number). Use type='temperature' to set temperature (value: numeric degrees). Use type='color_rgb' to change color (redValue, greenValue, blueValue: 0-255). The 'type' field is the discriminator — pick it based on what the user asked to change.

oneOf.description: Power capability: turn device on or off. Use ONLY when user wants to change power state.
Temperature capability: set temperature to a numeric value. Use when user wants to change temperature.

value.description: Brightness level as a number between 0 and 100

oneOf.description: Brightness capability: set brightness to a numeric value between 0 and 100. Use when user wants to change brightness.
Color RGB capability: set device color using red, green, blue channels (0-255 each). Use when user wants to change color.

deviceId.description: Device identifier. Prefer this when known; if provided, the tool uses it directly and does not need to look up the device by name.

deviceName.description: Device name. Use this only when deviceId is not known; the tool will look up the device by name before updating it.

vendor.description: Vendor used to decide where to route the request

inputSchema.description: Update one capability of a device. Provide deviceId when you already know the device; otherwise provide deviceName and the tool will look it up.

tools.name: update_device_capabilities

outputSchema.description: Tool response. On failure the response contains a structured error.
